package_info.why_malicious: The package contains heavily obfuscated JavaScript code that disables Windows Defender and other security protections, downloads and executes a known trojan/cryptominer, and attempts anti-forensics. The package is published by an untrustworthy account and masquerades as a legitimate utility, using deceptive tactics to evade detection and persist on infected systems.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when checker.js is loaded as part of the package)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Heavily obfuscated JavaScript code using JSDefender, which upon deobfuscation executes multiple Windows batch commands to disable security features.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Runs a series of batch commands to disable Windows Defender, tamper protection, real-time protection, and other security services by modifying registry keys and stopping services.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling security protections is a classic precursor to further malicious activity, such as malware installation or data theft. The use of obfuscation further indicates an attempt to evade detection and hinder analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate npm package should not attempt to alter system security settings, modify the Windows registry, or execute commands that impact system-wide security features.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise deployment scripts may disable security for compatibility, but never in a userland npm package distributed via the public registry.
key_indicators: Direct registry modifications targeting Defender and related keys
Batch commands to stop/disable security services
Execution of system-level commands at import-time

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads a trojanized Discord.exe binary from a Discord CDN link and places it in the Windows startup folder for persistence, ensuring the malicious payload is executed on system startup.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and persisting an unknown executable from a remote source is a hallmark of malware delivery. The use of the Windows startup folder for persistence is a well-known technique for ensuring malware runs automatically.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: npm packages should never download or install binaries outside their own directory, especially not to system startup locations or without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None in the context of a public npm package. Only specialized enterprise deployment tools, with explicit user consent, might perform similar actions.
key_indicators: Use of Discord CDN for malware hosting
Writes to Windows startup folder for persistence
No user interaction or consent for download or execution
Spawning shell commands to download and persist executables

execution_context.trigger: import-time (as part of checker.js execution, after Discord.exe drop)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a remove.cmd script from Discord CDN, which repeats the Defender-disabling commands for redundancy and to ensure security features remain disabled.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Redundant disabling of security features is a strong indicator of persistence and anti-detection intent. Downloading and executing remote scripts without user knowledge is a clear sign of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should download and execute remote scripts that alter system security, especially without user awareness or consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None in this context. Automated remote script execution is never appropriate in a public npm package.
key_indicators: Remote script execution from Discord CDN
Execution of downloaded scripts without validation

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when Discord.exe is executed at system startup)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: public static void Main() { ... encrypted payload ... }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Executes encrypted .NET code, likely a cryptominer or trojan, with the decryption key packed inside for runtime decryption and execution. The payload is designed to evade static analysis and may perform further malicious actions such as cryptomining or establishing remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Encrypted payloads in binaries are a common malware evasion technique. The use of Discord.exe as a filename is also suspicious, as it mimics legitimate software to avoid user suspicion.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not self-decrypt and execute hidden payloads, especially from a binary dropped by a third-party npm package.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some DRM or commercial software may use encryption for intellectual property protection, but not in the context of a dropped binary from an npm package.
key_indicators: Encrypted code blocks within the binary
Suspicious filename and delivery method (Discord.exe in startup folder)
Execution of payload without user knowledge

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the flame-vali npm package, triggering execution of checker.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: System security protections are disabled, opening the system to further compromise.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads and persists a trojanized Discord.exe binary to the Windows startup folder.
attack_chain.leads_to: Trojan will execute on next system startup, establishing persistence.

attack_chain.action: A remove.cmd script is downloaded and executed, redundantly disabling security features.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ensures security protections remain disabled, even if initial commands failed.

attack_chain.action: Discord.exe runs at startup, decrypts and executes its malicious payload (likely cryptominer/trojan).
attack_chain.leads_to: System is compromised, attacker achieves final goal (e.g., cryptomining, remote access, data theft).

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript in npm packages that spawns shell or batch commands at import-time
Batch commands targeting Windows Defender and registry keys for disabling security features
Network requests to Discord CDN for downloading executables or scripts
Dropping executables named Discord.exe to Windows startup folders for persistence
Execution of downloaded scripts (e.g., remove.cmd) without user consent
file_indicators: checker.js with obfuscated code in the package root
remove.cmd script in the working directory or temporary folder
Registry modifications under HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender and related subkeys
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for obfuscated JavaScript that spawns shell or batch commands, especially those modifying Windows Defender settings or downloading executables/scripts from Discord CDN. Flag any package that writes to Windows startup folders or drops binaries named Discord.exe. Alert on registry modifications under Windows Defender keys and on network requests to Discord CDN for suspicious file types such as .exe or .cmd. Correlate these behaviors to identify coordinated malicious activity.
